problem_markdown: For an interior point $P$ of triangle $ABC$, let $D,E,F$ be its perpendicular feet on $BC,CA,AB$. Determine all $P$ minimising $BC/PD+CA/PE+AB/PF$.
solutions_markdown:
Write $a=BC,b=CA,c=AB$ and $x=PD,y=PE,z=PF$. If the triangle's area is $\Delta$, then $ax+by+cz=2\Delta$. Cauchy–Schwarz gives
$$\left(\frac ax+\frac by+\frac cz\right)(ax+by+cz)\ge(a+b+c)^2.$$
Equality holds exactly when $x=y=z$. The unique interior point equidistant from all three sidelines is the incenter. Thus it uniquely minimises the expression, whose minimum is $(a+b+c)^2/(2\Delta)$.
